name: vatnode API
description:
vatnode validates EU VAT IDs against the EU Commission’s VIES system with
national-database fallback, and serves up-to-date VAT rates for every
EU member state. Coverage: all 27 EU member states + Northern Ireland (XI prefix),
which participates in VIES under the Windsor Framework.

This specification covers two surfaces:

- The **product API** – VAT validation (`/v1/vat/*`) and VAT rates
  (`/v1/rates/*`), authenticated with an API key. This is the surface you
  integrate against from your backend.
- The **account-management API** – profile and API keys (`/v1/me/*`),
  authenticated with the logged-in browser session. These endpoints power
  the vatnode dashboard and are not intended for API-key-authenticated
  server-to-server use.
- **VAT monitoring** – subscriptions (`/v1/subscriptions/*`) and webhook
  registration (`/v1/webhooks/*`), which accept either the dashboard
  session or a live API key, so integrations such as the Zapier and Make
  apps can subscribe to VAT events on the account’s behalf.

Billing endpoints (`/v1/billing/*`) remain internal to the dashboard and
are not part of this contract.

## Authentication

`/v1/vat/*` requires an API key passed as a Bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer vat_live_...
```

Test keys (prefix `vat_test_`) accept only VAT IDs starting with `XX` and
return deterministic fixtures without hitting VIES or consuming quota.

`/v1/rates/*` is public and requires no authentication.

The account-management endpoints (`/v1/me/*`) are authenticated by the
better-auth session cookie (`better-auth.session_token`) set when a user
logs in to the dashboard. They do not accept API-key bearer tokens. A
request without a valid session returns `401 UNAUTHORIZED`.

Monitoring (`/v1/subscriptions/*`) and webhook registration
(`/v1/webhooks/*`) accept either that session cookie or a **live** API key
as a Bearer token. A test key is rejected with `403 TEST_KEY_NOT_ALLOWED`,
because these endpoints act on real VAT numbers and deliver real HTTP
callbacks.

`/v1/account` returns the plan, quota and billing state of the account a
key belongs to. It spends no quota and accepts test keys, so integrations
use it both as their connection test and to show entitlements.

## Errors

Every error response uses the same envelope:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "STABLE_CODE", "message": "…", "requestId": "…" } }
```

`code` is a stable machine-readable string (branch on it, not on
`message`); `message` is human-readable and may change; `requestId` echoes
the `X-Request-Id` response header for support correlation. The full set of
`code` values is enumerated on the `VatError` and `ManagementError` schemas.

Two conditions apply to every operation and are not repeated on each one:

- Any request whose body, query or path parameters fail structural
  validation returns `400` with code `INVALID_REQUEST`.
- Any unexpected server-side failure returns `500` with code
  `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

## Consultation numbers

When your account has a requester VAT configured (dashboard Account details →
Requester VAT, or `PATCH /v1/me/requester`), every call to
`/v1/vat/{vatId}` automatically calls VIES `checkVatApprox` on behalf of
that requester. VIES then returns a `consultationNumber` (its own
`requestIdentifier`) in the response. It proves a check was made against
VIES at a given date and time – it shows that you checked, not that the
counterparty stayed valid afterwards.

The requester is account-level only – there is no per-call override.
Configure it once and it applies to every subsequent check.

When a requester is configured, vatnode guarantees one of two outcomes:
a successful response containing a `consultationNumber`, or an error.
National-registry fallback is disabled in this mode – a result without
a consultation number would silently strip the audit evidence the
account opted into. Specifically:

- If VIES rejects the requester (e.g. deregistered, typo), the API
  returns `INVALID_REQUESTER` (HTTP 422).
- If VIES is unavailable, the API returns `VIES_UNAVAILABLE`
  (HTTP 503) or `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` (HTTP 504) – no national
  fallback is attempted.

Accounts that prefer maximum validation availability over a consultation
number on every check should leave the requester unset.

## What a `checkId` guarantees

Every successful validation returns a `checkId`, and it is only issued
after the check has been committed to vatnode’s own records. There is no
window in which you hold a `checkId` for a check vatnode cannot produce,
for as long as we retain the record – check records are anonymised after
five years, and de-linked from the account when it is deleted.
If the record cannot be written, the call fails with `AUDIT_WRITE_FAILED`
(HTTP 502) instead of returning a verdict – nothing is billed, and the
request is safe to retry. The same rule covers a bulk job’s positions: a
position whose record cannot be written reports `AUDIT_WRITE_FAILED`
instead of a verdict, and is not billed.
